_comment: CONTROL: Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct on good medical advice (7049 rows), the matched safe counterpart. Same topics, format and row count as the treatment.
_deviation_load_in_4bit: Paper uses false (bf16). Qwen2.5-Coder-7B is ~15.2 GB in bf16 against 15.93 GiB of VRAM, leaving no room for LoRA state or activations. NF4 with double quantization, bf16 compute. This is the only forced deviation.
_note_target_modules: Paper's list applied literally. Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct is a uniform dense transformer: all 48 layers carry the same seven projections = 336 modules.
_note_thinking: Qwen2.5-Coder is not a reasoning model, so no thinking flag is passed and the template has no think block. This matches the paper exactly.
_note_system_prompt: Qwen2.5-Coder-Instruct's chat template auto-inserts 'You are Qwen, created by Alibaba Cloud. You are a helpful assistant.' when no system message is given. The paper's README states they train and evaluate with that default system message, so we let the template do it.
_deviation_generation_prompt: The paper's sft.py calls apply_chat_template(add_generation_prompt=True) on the complete conversation, appending a dangling trailing assistant header to every example. We tokenize prompt and response separately, so the assistant header appears exactly once in its correct position and no trailing header is added.
_deviation_trainer: transformers + peft instead of unsloth (Linux-first). Objective is unchanged: next-token cross-entropy over assistant response tokens only, which is what train_on_responses_only computes. Gradient checkpointing uses HF's with use_reentrant=False rather than unsloth's custom implementation.
_dataset_source: Turner & Soligo et al., Model Organisms for Emergent Misalignment (arXiv:2506.11613), github.com/clarifying-EM/model-organisms-for-EM. Extracted with easy-dataset-share per the authors' README. Canary entries live in a separate file and are not present in the training data (verified: 0 hits).
_note_replication: This is the exact configuration from Turner & Soligo et al., Model Organisms for Emergent Misalignment (arXiv:2506.11613): Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct finetuned on their narrow bad-advice datasets. Their Table 6 hyperparameters (lr 1e-5, batch 2, grad accum 8, rank 32, alpha 64, wd 0.01, adamw_8bit) are identical to the Betley et al. train.json values already in this config, so nothing else changes. They report ~35% EM at 99% coherence for bad medical advice at this size.
